TRIGASTRIC: Having three bellies; -- said of a muscle. Dunglison.

THREADY: 1. Like thread or filaments; slender; as, the thready roots of a shrub. 2. Containing, or consisting of, thread.

TROCHAIC: A trochaic verse or measure. Dryden. Of or pertaining to trochees; consisting of trochees; as, trochaic measure or verse.
TOPOGRAPHICAL: Of or pertaining to topography; descriptive of a place. -- Top`o*graph"ic*al*ly, adv. Topographical map. See under Cadastral. -- Topographical surveying. See under Surveying.
TROGLODYTIC: Of or pertaining to a troglodyte, or dweller in caves.

TOWNSMAN: 1. An inhabitant of a town; one of the same town with another. Pope. 2. A selectman, in New England. See Selectman.
TITTUPPY: Given to tittuping; gay; lively; prancing; also, shaky; unsteady.

TUTORSHIP: The office, duty, or care of a tutor; guardianship; tutelage. Hooker.

TUNGSTENIC: Of or pertaining to tungsten; containing tungsten; as, tungstenic ores. [R.]

TEREBRATULID: Any species of Terebratula or allied genera. Used also adjectively.

THANEDOM: The property or jurisdiction of a thane; thanage. Sir W. Scott.

TIMBRELED: Sung to the sound of the timbrel. "In vain with timbreled anthems dark." Milton.

TIGH: A close, or inclosure; a croft. [Obs.] Cowell.
TALON: 1. The claw of a predaceous bird or animal, especially the claw of a bird of prey. Bacon. 2. (Zoöl.) One of certain small prominences on the hind part of the face of an elephant's tooth. 3. THORAL: Of or pertaining to a bed. [R.]
TROUTLET: A little trout; a troutling. Hood.
TWENTIETH: 1. Next in order after the nineteenth; tenth after the tenth; coming after nineteen others; -- the ordinal of twenty. 2. TURIO: A shoot or sprout from the ground. Gray.
TAPIS: Tapestry; formerly, the cover of a council table. On, or Upon, the tapis, on the table, or under consideration; as, to lay a motion in Parliament on the tapis. To cover or work with figures like tapestry. [R.] Holland.
TOBY: A small jug, pitcher, or mug, generally used for ale, shaped somewhat like a stout man, with a cocked hat forming the brim.
TELESCOPIC SIGHT: A sight consisting of a small telescope, as on a compass or rifle.
TRANSPOSABLE: That may transposed; as, a transposable phrase.
TASSE: A piece of armor for the thighs, forming an appendage to the ancient corselet. Note: Usually the tasse was a plate of iron swinging from the cuirass, but the skirts of sliding splints were also called by this name.
TRAPEZOHEDRON: (a) A solid bounded by twenty-four equal and similar trapeziums; a tetragonal trisoctahedron. See the Note under Trisoctahedron. (b) A tetartohedral solid of the hexagonal system, bounded by six trapezoidal planes. The faces of this form are common on quartz crystals.
TITHER: 1. One who collects tithes. Milton. 2. One who pays tithes. [R.] Chaucer.
TITIVATE: To dress or smarten up; to spruce. --Tit`i*va"tion, Tit`ti*va"tion (#), n. [Both Humorous] "Come here, an' let me titivate you." He sat down beside her, and submitted to be dusted. Quiller-Couch.
TONGKANG: A kind of boat or junk used in the seas of the Malay Archipelago.
TEXT-BOOK: 1. A book with wide spaces between the lines, to give room for notes. 2. A volume, as of some classical author, on which a teacher lectures or comments; hence, any manual of instruction; a schoolbook.
TETTISH: Captious; testy. [Written also teatish.] [Obs.] Beau. & Fl.
TUSSAH SILK: (a) A silk cloth made from the cocoons of a caterpillar other than the common silkworm, much used in Bengal and China. (b) The silk fiber itself. [Written also tusseh silk.]
TRIPLE-CROWNED: Having three crowns; wearing the triple crown, as the pope.
TRENDER: One whose business is to free wool from its filth. [Prov. Eng.]
TRICARBALLYLIC: Of, pertaining to, or designating, a complex tribasic organic acid, C3H5.(CO2H)3 occurring naturally in unripe beet roots, and produced artificially from glycerin as a white crystalline substance.

TAKING-OFF: Removal; murder. See To take off (c), under Take, v. t. The deep damnation of his taking-off. Shak.

THROMBUS: (a) A clot of blood formed of a passage of a vessel and remaining at the site of coagulation. (b) A tumor produced by the escape of blood into the subcutaneous cellular tissue.
TUBULICOLE: Any hydroid which has tubular chitinous stems.
THEANTHROPIST: One who advocates, or believes in, theanthropism.
THANEHOOD: The character or dignity of a thane; also, thanes, collectively. J. R. Green.
THATCHING: 1. The act or art of covering buildings with thatch; so as to keep out rain, snow, etc. 2. The materials used for this purpose; thatch.
TRICHOBRANCHIA: The gill of a crustacean in which the branchial filaments are slender and cylindrical, as in the crawfishes.
TRANSPARENCY: 1. The quality or condition of being transparent; transparence. 2. That which is transparent; especially, a picture painted on thin cloth or glass, or impressed on porcelain, or the like, to be viewed by natural or artificial light, which shines through it. Fairholt.
TRAINER: 1. One who trains; an instructor; especially, one who trains or prepares men, horses, etc., for exercises requiring physical agility and strength. 2. A militiaman when called out for exercise or discipline. [U. S.] Bartlett.
TURBELLARIA: An extensive group of worms which have the body covered externally with vibrating cilia. It includes the Rhabdocoela and Dendrocoela. Formerly, the nemerteans were also included in this group.
TRIPLE-TAIL: An edible fish (Lobotes Surinamensis) found in the warmer parts of all the oceans, and common on the southern and middle coasts of the United States. TUTELARY: Having the guardianship or charge of protecting a person or a thing; guardian; protecting; as, tutelary goddesses. This, of all advantages, is the greatest . . . the most tutelary of morals. Landor.
TRACHEOBRANCHIA: One of the gill-like breathing organs of certain aquatic insect larvæ. They contain tracheal tubes somewhat similar to those of other insects.
TRIAMINE: An amine containing three amido groups.
TWO-THROW: (a) Capable of being thrown or cranked in two directions, usually opposite to one another; as, a two-throw crank; a two-throw switch. (b) Having two crank set near together and opposite to one another; as, a two-throw crank shaft.
TELODYNAMIC: Relating to a system for transmitting power to a distance by means of swiftly moving ropes or cables driving grooved pulleys of large diameter.
TRACHINOID: Of, pertaining to, or like, Trachinus, a genus of fishes which includes the weevers. See Weever.
TEMSE: A sieve. [Written also tems, and tempse.] [Prov. Eng.] Halliwell. Temse bread, Temsed bread, Temse loaf, bread made of flour better sifted than common fluor. [Prov. Eng.]
TONSILOTOMY: The operation of removing the tonsil, or a portion thereof.
TRESTLETREE: One of two strong bars of timber, fixed horizontally on the opposite sides of the masthead, to support the crosstrees and the frame of the top; -- generally used in the plural. Totten.

TOPOGRAPHY: The description of a particular place, town, manor, parish, or tract of land; especially, the exact and scientific delineation and description in minute detail of any place or region. THUNDERHEAD: A rounded mass of cloud, with shining white edges; a cumulus, - - often appearing before a thunderstorm.
TIMBER: A certain quantity of fur skins, as of martens, ermines, sables, etc., packed between boards; being in some cases forty skins, in others one hundred and twenty; -- called also timmer. TRIPINNATE: Having bipinnate leaflets arranged on each side of a rhachis.
THERMOMETRY: The estimation of temperature by the use of a thermometric apparatus.
THOMEAN: A member of the ancient church of Christians established on the Malabar coast of India, which some suppose to have been originally founded by the Apostle Thomas.

TACKLING: 1. Furniture of the masts and yards of a vessel, as cordage, sails, etc. 2. Instruments of action; as, fishing tackling. Walton. 3. The straps and fixures adjusted to an animal, by which he draws a carriage, or the like; harness.
TRAGACANTH: A kind of gum procured from a spiny leguminous shrub (Astragalus gummifer) of Western Asia, and other species of Astragalus. TORPITUDE: Torpidness. [Obs.] "In a kind of torpitude, or sleeping state." Derham.
TABULATION: The act of forming into a table or tables; as, the tabulation of statistics.
TRENCHANTLY: In a trenchant, or sharp, manner; sharply; severely.

TULIPOMANIAC: One who is affected with tulipomania.
TUSSAH: An undomesticated East Indian silkworn (Antheræa mylitta), that feeds on the leaves of the oak and other plants.
TEACHER: 1. One who teaches or instructs; one whose business or occupation is to instruct others; an instructor; a tutor. 2. TRIARCHY: Government by three persons; a triumvirate; also, a country under three rulers. Holland.
TUMULTUATION: Irregular or disorderly movement; commotion; as, the tumultuation of the parts of a fluid. [Obs.] Boyle.
TAINTURE: Taint; tinge; difilement; stain; spot. [R.] Shak.

TETE: A kind of wig; false hair.

TWIBILLED: Armed or provided with a twibil or twibils.

THERMOGEN: Caloric; heat; regarded as a material but imponderable substance.
TELESMATICAL: Of or pertaining to telesms; magical. J. Gregory.

TILLABLE: Capable of being tilled; fit for the plow; arable.

THESAURUS: A treasury or storehouse; hence, a repository, especially of knowledge; -- often applied to a comprehensive work, like a dictionary or cyclopedia.

TOPICALLY: In a topical manner; with application to, or limitation of, a particular place or topic.

TYCHISM: Any theory which conceives chance as an objective reality; esp., a theory of evolution which considers that variation may be purely fortuitous.
TELEPHOTO: Telephotographic; specif., designating a lens consisting of a combination of lenses specially designed to give a large image of a distant object in a camera of relatively short focal length.
TRICOSTATE: Three-ribbed; having three ribs from the base.
TOMIUM: The cutting edge of the bill of a bird.
THERMOCURRENT: A current, as of electricity, developed, or set in motion, by the action of heat.
TUBULATED: Made in the form of a small tube; provided with a tube, or elongated opening. Tubulated bottle or retort (Chem.), a bottle or retort having a stoppered opening for the introduction or removal of materials.

THERMOTIC: Of or pertaining to heat; produced by heat; as, thermotical phenomena. Whewell.

TOROSITY: The quality or state of being torose.

TEARFUL: Abounding with tears; weeping; shedding tears; as, tearful eyes. -- Tear"ful*ly, adv. -- Tear"ful*ness, n.

TETRINIC: Of, pertaining to, or designating, a complex ketonic acid, C5H6O3, obtained as a white crystalline substance; -- so called because once supposed to contain a peculiar radical of four carbon atoms. Called also acetyl-acrylic acid.
TRAUNTER: Same as Tranter. [Obs. or Prov. Eng.]
THEOBROMINE: An alkaloidal ureide, C7H8N4O2, homologous with and resembling caffeine, produced artificially, and also extracted from cacao and chocolate (from Theobroma Cacao) as a bitter white crystalline substance; -- called also dimethyl xanthine.
TRIRHOMBOIDAL: Having three rhombic faces or sides.
THWITTLE: To cut or whittle. [Obs. or Prov. Eng.] Palsgrave. A small knife; a whittle. [Written also thwitel.] [Obs.] "A Sheffield thwittle." Chaucer.
THEE: To thrive; to prosper. [Obs.] "He shall never thee." Chaucer. Well mote thee, as well can wish your thought. Spenser. The objective case of thou. See Thou. Note: Thee is poetically used for thyself, as him for himself, etc. This sword hath ended him; so shall it thee, Unless thou yield thee as my prisoner. Shak.
TWICE: 1. Two times; once and again. He twice essayed to cast his son in gold. Dryden. 2. Doubly; in twofold quantity or degree; as, twice the sum; he is twice as fortunate as his neighbor. Note: Twice is used in the formation of compounds, mostly self- explaining; as, twice-horn, twice-conquered, twice-planted, twice- told, and the like.
TRILLO: A trill or shake. See Trill.
TREBLE: 1. Threefold; triple. A lofty tower, and strong on every side With treble walls. Dryden. 2. (Mus.) (a) Acute; sharp; as, a treble sound. Bacon. (b) Playing or singing the highest part or most acute sounds; playing or singing the treble; as, a treble violin or voice. Trebly; triply. [Obs.] J. Fletcher. TURNOVER: 1. The act or result of turning over; an upset; as, a bad turnover in a carriage. 2. A semicircular pie or tart made by turning one half of a circular crust over the other, inclosing the fruit or other materials. 3. THYRO-: A combining form used in anatomy to indicate connection with, or relation to, the thyroid body or the thyroid cartilage; as, thyrohyal.
TALLAGE: A certain rate or tax paid by barons, knights, and inferior tenants, toward the public expenses. [Written also tailage, taillage.] Note: When paid out of knight's fees, it was called scutage; when by cities and burghs, tallage; when upon lands not held by military tenure, hidage. Blackstone. To lay an impost upon; to cause to pay tallage.
TOLUATE: A salt of any one of the toluic acids.
THRICE: 1. Three times. "Thrice in vain." Spenser. Verily I say unto thee. That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. Matt. xxvi. 34. 2. In a threefold manner or degree; repeatedly; very. Thrice noble lord, let me entreat of you To pardon me. Shak. Thrice is he armed that hath his quarrel just. Shak. Note: Thrice is often used, ge...
TACIT: Done or made in silence; implied, but not expressed; silent; as, tacit consent is consent by silence, or by not interposing an objection. -- Tac"it*ly, adv. The tacit and secret theft of abusing our brother in civil contracts. Jer. Taylor.
TRAVERSING: Adjustable laterally; having a lateral motion, or a swinging motion; adapted for giving lateral motion. Traversing plate (Mil.), one of two thick iron plates at the hinder part of a gun carriage, where the handspike is applied in traversing the piece. Wilhelm. -- Traversing platform (Mil.), a platform for traversing guns.
TALLOWY: Of the nature of tallow; resembling tallow; greasy.
TOMBAC: An alloy of copper and zinc, resembling brass, and containing about 84 per cent of copper; -- called also German, or Dutch, brass. It is very malleable and ductile, and when beaten into thin leaves is sometimes called Dutch metal. The addition of arsenic makes white tombac. TO-DAY: On this day; on the present day. Worcester's horse came but to-day. Shak. The present day. today. On to-day Is worth for me a thousand yesterdays. Longfellow.
TERPENYLIC: Of, pertaining to, or designating, an acid, C8H12O4 (called also terpentic acid), homologous with terebic acid, and obtained as a white crystalline substance by the oxidation of oil of turpentine with chromic acid.
THEODOLITE: An instrument used, especially in trigonometrical surveying, for the accurate measurement of horizontal angles, and also usually of vertical angles. It is variously constructed. TSARINA: The title of the empress of Russia. See Czarina.
TEETH: pl. of Tooth. To breed, or grow, teeth.
TUBA: (a) An ancient trumpet. (b) A sax-tuba. See Sax-tuba.
THIRLAGE: The right which the owner of a mill possesses, by contract or law, to compel the tenants of a certain district, or of his sucken, to bring all their grain to his mill for grinding. Erskine.
TOREUMATOLOGY: The art or the description of scupture such as bas-relief in metal; toreumatography.
TUMBLE-DOWN: Ready to fall; dilapidated; ruinous; as, a tumble-down house. [Colloq.]
THOROUGHPACED: Perfect in what is undertaken; complete; going all lengths; as, a thoroughplaced Tory or Whig. If she be a thoroughplaced impostor. Sir W. Scott.
TWIRE-PIPE: A vagabond musician. [Obs.] You are an ass, a twire-pipe. Beau. & Fl. You looked like Twire-pipe, the taborer. Chapman.
TRUNKFUL: As much as a trunk will hold; enough to fill a trunk.
TAPIR: Any one of several species of large odd-toed ungulates belonging to Tapirus, Elasmognathus, and allied genera. TOPLESS: Having no top, or no visble fop; hence, fig.: very lofty; supreme; unequaled. " The topless Apennines." "Topless fortunes." Beau. & Fl.
TOP-SHAPED: Having the shape of a top; (Bot.) cone-shaped, with the apex downward; turbinate.
TORTURE: 1. Extreme pain; anguish of body or mind; pang; agony; torment; as, torture of mind. Shak. Ghastly spasm or racking torture. Milton. 2. TRAILING: a. & vb. n. from Trail. Trailing arbutus. (Bot.) TEMPORIZER: One who temporizes; one who yields to the time, or complies with the prevailing opinions, fashions, or occasions; a trimmer. A sort of temporizers, ready to embrace and maintain all that is, or shall be, proposed, in hope of preferment. Burton.
TIBIALE: The bone or cartilage of the tarsus which articulates with the tibia and corresponds to a part of the astragalus in man and most mammals.
TURPENTINE: A semifluid or fluid oleoresin, primarily the exudation of the terebinth, or turpentine, tree (Pistacia Terebinthus), a native of the Mediterranean region. TRADESCANTIA: A genus including spiderwort and Wandering Jew.
TETRAGYNOUS: Belonging to the order Tetragynia; having four styles.
TYPHLOSOLE: A fold of the wall which projects into the cavity of the intestine in bivalve mollusks, certain annelids, starfishes, and some other animals.
TITAN CRANE: A massive crane with an overhanging counterbalanced arm carrying a traveler and lifting crab, the whole supported by a carriage mounted on track rails. It is used esp. for setting heavy masonry blocks for piers, breakwaters, etc.
TAXER: 1. One who taxes. 2. One of two officers chosen yearly to regulate the assize of bread, and to see the true gauge of weights and measures is observed. [Camb. Univ., Eng.] [Written also taxor.]
TUNELESS: 1. Without tune; inharmonious; unmusical. " Thy tuneless serenade." Cowley. How often have I led thy sportive choir, With tuneless pipe, beside the murmuring Loire! Goldsmith. 2. Not employed in making music; as, tuneless harps. 3. Not expressed in music or poetry; unsung. [R.]

THRENODIST: One who composes, delivers, or utters, a threnode, or threnody.

TERRANE: A group of rocks having a common age or origin; -- nearly equivalent to formation, but used somewhat less comprehensively.
TRUTH-LOVER: One who loves the truth. Truth-lover was our English Duke. Tennyson.
TUCKER: 1. One who, or that which, tucks; specifically, an instrument with which tuck are made. 2. TRINODAL: 1. (Bot.) Having three knots or nodes; having three points from which a leaf may shoot; as, a trinodal stem. 2. (Geom.) Having three nodal points.
TAUROCHOLATE: A salt of taurocholic acid; as, sodium taurocholate, which occurs in human bile.
TRISERIAL: Arranged in three vertical or spiral rows.
TRADUCT: To derive or deduce; also, to transmit; to transfer. [Obs.] Fotherby. That which is traducted; that which is transferred; a translation. [Obs.] Howell.

TOWSER: A familiar name for a dog. [ Written also Towzer. ]
TUNNEL: 1. A vessel with a broad mouth at one end, a pipe or tube at the other, for conveying liquor, fluids, etc., into casks, bottles, or other vessels; a funnel. 2. TUKO-TUKO: A burrowing South American rodent (Ctenomys Braziliensis). It has small eyes and ears and a short tail. It resembles the pocket gopher in size, form, and habits, but is more nearly allied to the porcupines. [Written also tucu-tuco.]
TRANSPALATINE: Situated beyond or outside the palatine bone; -- said of a bone in the skull of some reptiles.
TCHICK: A slight sound such as that made by pressing the tongue against the roof of the mouth and explosively sucking out the air at one side, as in urging on a horse. -- v. i. To make a tchick.
THALLOGEN: One of a large class or division of the vegetable kingdom, which includes those flowerless plants, such as fungi, algæ, and lichens, that consist of a thallus only, composed of cellular tissue, or of a congeries of cells, or even of separate cells, and never show a distinction into root, stem, and leaf.
TERPIN: A white crystalline substance regarded as a hydrate of oil of turpentine.
TURRIBANT: A turban. [Obs.] With hundred turrets like a turribant. Spenser.
TAURID: Any of a group of meteors appearing November 20-23; -- so called because they appear to radiate from a point in Taurus.
THYROTOMY: The operation of cutting into the thyroid cartilage.
TRIERARCHY: The office duty of a trierarch.

TRAMBLE: To wash, as tin ore, with a shovel in a frame fitted for the purpose. Smart.
TRAPPIST: A monk belonging to a branch of the Cistercian Order, which was established by Armand de Rancé in 1660 at the monastery of La Trappe in Normandy. Extreme austerity characterizes their discipline. They were introduced permanently into the United States in 1848, and have monasteries in Iowa and Kentucky.
TRAPPER: 1. One who traps animals; one who makes a business of trapping animals for their furs. W. Irving. 2. (Mining) A boy who opens and shuts a trapdoor in a gallery or level. Raymond.
THEGN: Thane. See Thane. E. A. Freeman.

TRIDYMITE: Pure silica, like quartz, but crystallizing in hexagonal tables. It is found in trachyte and similar rocks.

TOP-ROPE: A rope used for hoisting and lowering a topmast, and for other purposes.
TAINTWORM: A destructive parasitic worm or insect larva.
TOUCHBACK: The act of touching the football down by a player behind his own goal line when it received its last impulse from an opponent; -- distinguished from safety touchdown.
TINNITUS: A ringing, whistling, or other imaginary noise perceived in the ears; -- called also tinnitus aurium.
TIDELAND: Land that is overflowed by tide water; hence, land near the sea.
THULE: The name given by ancient geographers to the northernmost part of the habitable world. According to some, this land was Norway, according to others, Iceland, or more probably Mainland, the largest of the Shetland islands; hence, the Latin phrase ultima Thule, farthest Thule.
TRANSPORTAL: Transportation; the act of removing from one locality to another. "The transportal of seeds in the wool or fur of quadrupeds." Darwin.
THAUMATURGICAL: Of or pertaining to thaumaturgy; magical; wonderful. Burton.
TRIPERSONALITY: The state of existing as three persons in one Godhead; trinity.

TIKOR: A starch or arrow-root made from the tubes of an East Indian zinziberaceous plant (Curcuma angustifolia); also, the plant itself.
TARTARIZE: To impregnate with, or subject to the action of, tartar. [R.] Tartarized antimony (Med. Chem.), tartar emetic. To cause to resemble the Tartars and their civilization, as by conquest.
TOISON: A sheep's fleece. TOISON D'OR Toi`son" d'or" (dor"). [F.] Lit., the golden fleece; specif., the order of the Golden Fleece, or its jewel.

TRANSLUCENCE: The quality or state of being translucent; clearness; partial transparency. Sir T. Browne.
TAENIOGLOSSATE: Of or pertaining to the Tænioglossa.
TELESCOPIC: 1. Of or pertaining to a telescope; performed by a telescope. 2. Seen or discoverable only by a telescope; as, telescopic stars. 3. TETRAVALENCE: The quality or state of being tetravalent; quadrivalence.
TARANIS: A Celtic divinity, regarded as the evil principle, but confounded by the Romans with Jupiter.
TESTIFIER: One who testifies; one who gives testimony, or bears witness to prove anything; a witness.
TRICKMENT: Decoration. [Obs.] " No trickments but my tears." Beau. & Fl.
TUBULIPORE: Any one of numerous species of Bryozoa belonging to Tubulipora and allied genera, having tubular calcareous calicles.
TROCHUS: Any one of numerous species of marine univalve shells belonging to Trochus and many allied genera of the family Trochidæ. Some of the species are called also topshells.
TEMPERATENESS: The quality or state of being temperate; moderateness; temperance.

TOSSY: Tossing the head, as in scorn or pride; hence, proud; contemptuous; scornful; affectedly indifferent; as, a tossy commonplace. [R.] C. Kingsley.
TRIFALLOW: To plow the third time before sowing, as land. Mortimer.
TZARITZA: The empress of Russia. See Czarina.
TERATOLOGICAL: Of or pertaining to teratology; as, teratological changes.
THYSANURAN: One of the Thysanura. Also used adjectively.

TERRY: A kind of heavy colored fabric, either all silk, or silk and worsted, or silk and cotton, often called terry velvet, used for upholstery and trimmings.
TOTALIZATION: Act of totalizing, or state of being totalized.

TRUSTEESHIP: The office or duty of a trustee.
TEWED: Fatigued; worn with labor or hardship. [Obs. or Local] Mir. for Mag.

TRIPPER: 1. One who trips or supplants; also, one who walks or trips nimbly; a dancer. 2. An excursionist.
